content.text:
Finding submitted.

**Classification: deviation (critical) — § 13.4 fails the LOL-CAP fallback on three material terms.**

What I found across the responsive locations:
- **§ 13.4 (p0207)** — the only cap. It limits *M&I's* liability only, at **three months'** payments. That is both one-sided (Customer uncapped) and below the 6-month walk-away floor. Its sole exception is collection of amounts due.
- **§§ 11.1 / 11.2(A) (p0187, p0189)** — the Termination for Convenience and Cause Fees are expressly *outside* § 13.4, reinforcing the asymmetry (quantum itself left to the liquidated-damages rule, not double-flagged).
- **§ 13.2 (p0205)** — mutual indirect/consequential waiver is already in place, so no edit needed there.
- **§ 14.2 (indemnities)** and **§ 17.3–17.4 (confidentiality)** — no super-cap or carve-out language anywhere; indemnities sit inside the cap.
- **§ 22.16 (p0304)** — negotiated-limitations construction clause; does not cure anything.

Cure chosen at **fallback**, two surgical operations: change "M&I's" to "each party's" and "three (3)" to "twelve (12)" in the existing sentence (all other words verbatim), plus one short carve-out sentence for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and willful misconduct. I did not volunteer the preferred USD 1,000,000 greater-of floor, the data-protection/fraud/IP carve-outs, or the payment-obligations exclusion, since the fallback is a sufficient landing zone.
